items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: The final Monk record for Columbia which was the Oliver Nelson arrangements I thought just lost the whole spirit of Monk so badly that it was not a good record.

ctx.x: Right. Well it’s funny, it’s almost the same thing with rock bands. They have a hit and people want to hear it, but those things are fortunate for the bands I think. Did you feel good about what happened with Cannonball’s music and career in later years when he was with Capitol and so forth?

Well it’s funny, the answer always has to be yes and no. Because I’ll always — if I look at somebody who went on and it happened to practically everybody. I mean for instance if you ask me that question about Wes Montgomery I would have no trouble saying definitely not did I think that what happened to Wes was terrible and very possibly shortened his life because I know that he was pretty uptight about being put into this pop bag and playing all these heavily arranged and pop-derived material but Cannon pretty…

him up a notch to a major label, and he was pulled away from us. And I didn’t think anything sensible or helpful or intelligent was done to his career subsequently. Bill Evans also went on to a — although there what happened was he kind of knew that he was kind of good in the sense that even though when Bill first went to Verve, and that was a matter of Bill left Riverside with a year to go on his contract which was because we were in existence, we were starting to have real money problems and frankly Bill had…
